items.q: Do all religions believe exactly the same things?
items.correct: No — they share some ideas but differ significantly in beliefs and practices.
items.misconception: Yes, all religions are basically identical.
items.random_wrong: No two religions have anything in common.
items.why: Religious studies examines both similarities and important differences.

items.q: Do you have to be religious to study Religious Studies?
items.correct: No — RS examines beliefs, practices and ethics academically.
items.misconception: Yes, only believers can study it.
items.random_wrong: RS is only about memorising prayers.
items.why: You analyse and evaluate viewpoints; you don't have to hold them.

items.q: Does everyone within a religion believe identically?
items.correct: No — there is diversity within every religion (denominations, interpretations).
items.misconception: Yes, all followers believe exactly the same.
items.random_wrong: Diversity only exists between religions, never within.
items.why: Within any faith there are varied traditions, interpretations and practices.

items.q: Do ethical and religious questions have one fact to memorise?
items.correct: No — RS asks you to evaluate different viewpoints and justify reasoning.
items.misconception: Yes, there is always one correct answer to learn.
items.random_wrong: Reasons and evidence don't matter in RS.
items.why: Good answers weigh arguments and reach justified conclusions.
